1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 05.02.2020 passed in MVC.No.245/2018 by Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Gundlupet, (for short the 'Tribunal') the present appeal is filed by the petitioner therein for enhancement of compensation awarded.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that, on 11.06.2018 at about 1.30 p.m., the petitioner and his mother were going in motor bike bearing registration No.KA-10-V-8209, near cauvery comfort hotel,
Gundlupet - Calicut main road, Gundlupet, at that time, a car bearing registration No.KA-42-A-8298 being driven in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the motor bike and caused the accident.

Due to the accident, the petitioner sustained following injuries:-
i. Communitated fracture of left femur.
4. The Tribunal based on the evidence let-in came to the conclusion that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle which was duly insured with respondent No.3 and respondent No.3 is liable to pay a sum of Rs.4,10,620/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum under the following heads:

1. Expenditure of medicines 92,900 Shri Rajashekhar vs Shri Arun C on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63925050/
2  and treatment  2. Expenditure of food and 10,000  nourishment
3 . Expenditure of transportation 10,000  and attending charges
4. Loss of earning during the 10,000  treatment  5.
Future medical expenses 25,000  6. Loss of future earning on 2,52,720  account of permanent  disability  7. Pain and suffering 10,000  Total 4,10,620 5.
Not satisfied by the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
6. The accident occurred in the year 2018.
The income of the petitioner has not been established before the Tribunal.
Hence, the notional income as prescribed in the Lok-Adalath chart has to be considered, which will be Rs.12,500/- per month.

The doctor has opined that he has sustained 40%
permanent disability to the left leg lower limb and the Tribunal has taken whole body disability at 13%, which in my opinion is just and fair.
The petitioner was aged 24 years at the time of accident.

Hence, the multiplier of '18' has to be adopted as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. D.T.C [2009(6) SCC 121], thus the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.3,51,000/-(Rs.12,500x12x18x13%) towards 'loss of future income' as against Rs.2,52,720/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

Given the nature of injuries, the laid up period has to be considered as 3 months and the loss of income during the laid up period will be Rs.37,500/- (Rs.12,500x3) as against Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Towards the head 'loss of amenities', given the nature of injuries, I deem it appropriate to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-.
Towards pain and suffering, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem it appropriate to enhance it to Rs.40,000/-.
Towards medical expenses, based on the actual bills, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.92,900/-, which I deem it correct.

Towards transportation, attendant charges,
food and nourishment charges, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal, I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards the head 'future medical expenses, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem the same to be appropriate.

7. Thus, the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.5,96,400/- as described in the table below:

1. Expenditure of 92,900 92,900 medicines and treatment 2. Expenditure of 10,000 10,000 food and nourishment 3. Expenditure of 10,000 10,000 transportation and attending charges 4. Loss of earning 10,000 37,500 during the treatment 5.
Future medical 25,000 25,000 expenses 6. Loss of future 2,52,720 3,51,000 earning on account of permanent disability 7.
Pain and suffering 10,000 40,000 8. Loss of amenities NIL 30,000

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.5,96,400/- as against the compensation of Rs.4,10,620/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
Given the bank rate, it would be appropriate to award 6% per annum interest on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition before Tribunal till realization.
